name: K-Scale Z-Bot / K-Bot
description: Two open-source humanoids from K-Scale Labs: Z-Bot, a $999 entry-level hobbyist platform, and K-Bot, a full-size $9,000–$11,000 personal robot. Both ship with open hardware and software stacks for developers.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: ~77 lb — K-Bot only; Z-Bot's weight not published

specs.label: Height
specs.note: ~4'7" — K-Bot only; Z-Bot's height not published

sourcing: Specs sourced from Interesting Engineering's coverage of K-Bot's November 2025 initial release and K-Scale Labs' own GitHub repository, as of September 2026. Pricing for K-Bot has been reported inconsistently across sources ($8,999–$10,999) — treat the figure above as approximate. robotindex does not sell this product.

pricing.summary: Z-Bot is **$999**, while K-Bot runs roughly **$9,000–$11,000** depending on when it's priced, with a $100 refundable deposit for early reservations. Full autonomy is only a stated future goal — K-Scale has projected it for around 2028 — with initial units shipping in a more limited, app-controlled state.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: K-Bot ships with an **RGB camera and stereo vision** for an ultra-wide field of view, farfield microphones with stereo speakers, and a modular, upgradable sensor and compute suite with swappable end effectors. Both K-Bot and Z-Bot share K-Scale's open-source stack, with hardware released under CERN-OHL-S and software under GPL v3.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: K-Bot and Z-Bot ship under genuinely open licenses — hardware under CERN-OHL-S and software under GPL v3 — with K-Scale's own repositories publicly available on GitHub. That's a real openness commitment in a humanoid-robot category where most competitors keep both hardware and firmware closed, though K-Scale's own repo currently labels the release status "public alpha."
